title: Eight real incidents from building this lab
prescribes: After delivery, capture what worked, what did not and what to do differently -- with specific incidents rather than sentiments, so the lesson is transferable.
applied: Logged every failure encountered while building the lab into the skill's retrospective template, including the two negative results and the one analysis error.
narrative: 8 incidents, and the pattern is that 5 of them were environment or upstream drift rather than analysis mistakes. Skills that ship code age against their dependencies; the lesson is a compatibility shim, not distrust of the skill.

The one genuine analysis error is worth naming plainly: the campaign economics valued a saved customer at one year of margin in the threshold sweep and at lifetime value in the impact calculation, which made the same campaign look both unprofitable and profitable. The fix was one function used by both -- the same 'one metric, one definition' rule that `metric-reconciliation` teaches in phase 2, applied to our own work.

Two negative results were kept rather than deleted: the reranker that did not help, and the Bayesian search that tied with random search. A demonstration that only shows techniques winning is a brochure.

tables.title: Retrospective
rows: Making every demo return one dataclass meant the site needed exactly one renderer.
Define the shared economics before writing any phase that spends money -- the LTV inconsistency cost a rerun of phase 5.
Running the skills' own bundled scripts on real data found three upstream incompatibilities that reading the code would not have.
Check every bundled script against the installed library versions up front rather than discovering it mid-phase.
The coverage gate (46 artifacts or the build fails) removed any temptation to quietly skip a skill.
Size the heavy tracks by wall clock first; the CPU-only torch build shaped every later decision and was discovered by accident.
Seeding once in lib/seeds and importing it everywhere made phases 3-5 rerun to identical numbers.
